key_insight: Tether lets robots autonomously generate useful, task-directed experience by learning correspondences between past and current states and warping trajectories accordingly, enabling robust policies that generalize to diverse/out-of-distribution states.
problem_solved: How to continuously produce informative robot experience and train policies that remain robust across diverse, potentially out-of-distribution environment states without relying on dense human demonstrations.
method: Learn cross-state correspondences (visual or latent) between previously successful trajectories and the robot's current scene.
Warp and adapt stored trajectories to new contexts using the learned correspondences, producing task-directed synthetic demonstrations.
Use the warped trajectories in a closed-loop autonomous play pipeline to self-supervise a goal-conditioned policy and collect continual, useful experience.
impact: Enables scalable, demo-light robot learning by automating meaningful data collection and improving generalization; practical for practitioners building continual learning and manipulation systems.
visual_elements: Schematic: source trajectory mapped to target scene via correspondence-driven warping (before/after overlay).
Closed-loop diagram of autonomous play: warp → execute → collect → update policy.
Performance chart: success rate or task coverage vs autonomous play steps (showing improvement).
Heatmap/visualization of correspondences (pixel or latent mappings) between scenes.
paper_title: Tether: Autonomous Functional Play with Correspondence-Driven Trajectory Warping
paper_authors: William Liang, Sam Wang, Hung-Ju Wang, Osbert Bastani, Yecheng Jason Ma
